title: Heterogeneous Catalysis Surface Adsorption
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Chemistry
description: Step-through diagram of heterogeneous catalysis using the Haber process on an iron surface. Seven steps show adsorption, bond breaking, stepwise N-H bond formation, and desorption with atoms conserved, and a slider shows how cutting the same iron into smaller pieces increases the number of surface atoms that act as active sites.

learningObjectives: Identify the adsorption, surface reaction, and desorption stages of heterogeneous catalysis
Explain why a catalyst is not consumed and why it lowers the activation energy
Explain why the surface area of a solid catalyst affects the reaction rate
prerequisites: Effect of a catalyst on a reaction energy diagram
standards: AP Chemistry CED Unit 5, Topic 5.11: Catalysis

controls.label: Next Step
controls.description: Moves forward one step through the seven steps

controls.label: Show Labels
controls.description: Shows or hides the labels in the picture and the explanation of the step

controls.label: Iron cut into pieces
controls.description: Cuts a block of 144 iron atoms into 1, 4, 9, 16, or 36 pieces and counts the surface atoms

controls.label: Stage tabs
controls.description: Clicking a stage tab jumps to the first step of that stage

equations: Surface atoms of a k by k piece = 4k - 4 (1 if k = 1)
assumptions: Schematic side view of the surface: atom sizes and positions are not to scale
The surface area panel is a two-dimensional cross-section of 12 by 12 atoms

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through worked example with a hide-the-labels self-check
keyQuestions: What happens to the bonds in the reactant molecules when they are adsorbed?
How can you tell from the picture that the catalyst is not consumed?
Why does a fine powder have more active sites than a solid block of the same mass?
commonMisconceptions: Believing the catalyst is used up or becomes part of the product
Believing a catalyst changes the enthalpy change or the equilibrium position
Believing every atom in a solid catalyst takes part, not only the surface atoms
assessmentOpportunities: With labels hidden, have students name the stage and describe the bonds breaking and forming in a chosen step
